target: new: colour of a marking (streaked FLOPO:0991206, the streaks purple PATO_0000951)
reason: Two facts: the part is streaked (FLOPO:0991206), and the streaks, not the whole part, are purple. Putting purple on the bearer would be wrong, so the colour has to sit on the marking.
epruinose = without a waxy bloom. It is the negation of pruinose, which the previous review mapped to PATO_0104277 glaucous (C222).

target: new: cross-section shape (pentagonal PATO_0040016 and grooved PATO_0002255, in transverse section)
reason: A shape stated 'in T.S.' (in cross-section): five-angled with grooved faces. Both values hold at once, so this is not a continuum, and the transverse section is a view of the bearer, not part of the quality.
A transcription fragment ('... mixed with simple, spreading hairs'). The hair type it is mixed with is missing.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound X-Y continuum: flattened PATO_0002254 - terete PATO_0104016)
reason: A compound of two values: terete but somewhat flattened, between terete and flattened. This is the continuum reading of 'X-Y' compounds.

'apiculate' is an EXACT synonym of PATO_0000944 in the PATO lexicon, and 'abruptly' only says how the point arises. Mapping it to an attribute is a weak grounding; a FLOPO 'apiculate' value beside FLOPO:0991054 mucronate would be better, but that is a question about apiculate, not about this phrase.
bacilliform = rod-shaped, which is an EXACT synonym of PATO_0001873 cylindrical. Anthers, hairs and moss cells all use it in this sense.
Being widest above the middle is what defines obovate (plane shapes) and obovoid (solids) in the Systematics Association chart. The bearer decides which of the two applies.
A transcription fragment. What covers the part ('resinous glands') is cut off, and that covering is the quality (same as rejected C240 'covered').

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: vascular bundle PO_0005020 of the petal, colour brownish purple)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins of the petal, not to the petal. So this is a part of the bearer with a colour, not a new value.
gland-dotted with a density adverb. 'densely' is a degree qualifier for the record, not part of the value.
Same as rule C312 for rhomboidal. 'irregularly' is an approximation qualifier (pattern 01).
These are pores in the hyaline cell walls of Sphagnum leaves, not stomatal pores (PO_0008032). No PO or FLOPO class exists for them; one would need a moss anatomy class first.
Normal developmental breakdown of moss cells (cortex, columella). PATO_0000639 degenerate is defined as a pathological process, so it does not fit, and a new term would be doubtful from 8 statements.

label: heliophilous
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing in open places exposed to full sunlight rather than in shade.
reason: Light-demanding versus shade-tolerant is a standard trait in tropical forest floras. Like epiphytic and saxicolous (FLOPO:0991110, FLOPO:0991317), it is a habitat quality that is probably outside PATO's scope; PATO_0040029 shaded is a physical state, not a growth preference.
sublamellate / sublamelliform = almost plate-like: laminar (in the form of a thin plate) with the 'sub' prefix as an approximate value (pattern 01).
'non en forme de capuchon' is the negation of cucullate (hood-shaped), FLOPO:0991119.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound X-Y continuum: ovate PATO_0001891 - rhomboid PATO_0001938)
reason: A compound of two plane shapes, between ovate and rhomboid. This is the standard continuum reading.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound X-Y: acuminate PATO_0002228, obtuse PATO_0001935)
reason: An acuminate apex whose tip is blunt ('acuminé-obtus au sommet'): a compound of two apex values. No single term covers it.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: trichome PO_0000282 of the part, star shaped PATO_0002065)
reason: 'Stellate' is the shape of the hairs, not of the fruit or sepal (see flora_rejected_bearer_words 'stellate'). The part is hairy, and its trichomes are star-shaped.
PATO has the compound itself: deltoid is an EXACT synonym of triangular, so lanceolate-deltoid = PATO_0002338 lanceolate-triangular.
Unlike bare 'paler' (rejected C241), the second term here is implicit: the lower surface is paler than the upper. That is a discolorous blade.
'non unies à la base' = not united at the base. This is the 'free' rule for 'separate' (C178), with 'at base' as the region of the bearer.

torus (and tori) are synonyms of receptacle PO_0009064, so 'torus glabrous' describes the receptacle. 'disque en bourrelet' (a disc forming a ring-shaped swelling) is the disc's shape and should not be grounded here.

label: semi-hard
definition: A hardness quality inhering in a bearer, typically wood, by virtue of the bearer's being intermediate in hardness between soft and hard.
reason: The tender / semi-hard / hard classes are standard in tropical timber descriptions. PATO has hard (PATO_0000386) and soft (PATO_0000387) but nothing in between. The 'seed: bois demi-dur' row is a bearer error (the wood is meant).
microapiculate = minutely apiculate, and 'apiculate' is the EXACT synonym of PATO_0000944. It takes the same grounding as 'abruptly apiculate'.
'compound raceme' is a synonym of PO_0030116. The inflorescence type is a PO class, not a quality.
Latin scandens = scandent, climbing: 'Frutex scandens' is a climbing shrub.

label: pseudostipitate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's base being narrowed into a stalk-like portion that is part of the bearer itself rather than a distinct stalk.
reason: It is not stipitate (FLOPO:0991065, which is an attachment by a true stalk) and says more than 'tapered'. Same model as FLOPO:0991274 pseudopeltate.
Woolly hairs: 'woolly' is a synonym of PATO_0104357 lanate.
